sentence.ja: {私[わたし]}は日本人[にほんじん]です。
sentence.en: I'm Japanese.

mnemonic.story: Who's that on the *water ski*, spraying the whole lake? **I** am! You jab a thumb at your own chest a second before you wipe out. Watashi: I.

sentence.ja: {僕[ぼく]}は猫[ねこ]が大好[だいす]きです。
sentence.en: I love cats.

mnemonic.story: A small boy thumps his chest and lists *beaucoup* reasons he is the best: **I** can whistle, I can jump, I can burp the alphabet. Boku: I, said by boys and men.

sentence.ja: {あなた}も学生[がくせい]ですか。
sentence.en: Are you a student too?

mnemonic.story: At the aquarium *an otter* presses its paw to the glass and points straight at **you**, whiskers twitching. Anata: you, though Japanese usually uses your name instead.

sentence.ja: {彼[かれ]}は毎朝[まいあさ]走[はし]っています。
sentence.en: He goes running every morning.

mnemonic.story: **He** leans on his rusty *car*, grinning: '*Car, eh*?' and waits for you to admire the dented door. Kare: he; it also means boyfriend.

sentence.ja: {彼女[かのじょ]}はとても親切[しんせつ]な人[ひと]です。
sentence.en: She is a very kind person.

mnemonic.story: **She** glides past in a red *canoe* with *Jo* painted on the side, her paddle dripping. Kanojo: she; it also means girlfriend.

sentence.ja: ケンさんは私[わたし]の{友達[ともだち]}です。
sentence.en: Ken is my friend.

mnemonic.story: Your new **friend** turns up with a *tomato* in one hand and a *dach*shund under the other arm, and the dog licks the juice off your fingers. Tomo-dachi: friend.

sentence.ja: あの{人[ひと]}はだれですか。
sentence.en: Who is that person?

mnemonic.story: On a packed train a **person** plants a heel on your foot and you squeal "*Hee! Toe!*" Every head turns. Hito: person, the same 人 you read jin in nihonjin.

sentence.ja: ドアの前[まえ]に{男[おとこ]の人[ひと]}がいます。
sentence.en: There's a man in front of the door.

mnemonic.story: A **man** called *Otto* runs a one-man *Co.* from his garage, and the sign above the door reads OTTO CO. Otoko is man; otoko no hito, "man person", is the polite way to say it.

sentence.ja: あの{女[おんな]の人[ひと]}はだれですか。
sentence.en: Who is that woman?

mnemonic.story: The **woman** behind the café counter is the *owner*, and she flips the sign to OPEN herself, keys jangling. Onna is woman; onna no hito, "woman person", is the polite way to say it.

sentence.ja: {子供[こども]}は何時[なんじ]に寝[ね]ますか。
sentence.en: What time do the kids go to bed?

breakdown.baseEn: to sleep, to go to bed

mnemonic.story: A **child** at the bakery counter squeezes a lump of *cold dough* and shouts "*More!*", flour puffing up like smoke. Kodomo: child.

sentence.ja: クラスの{みんな}はやさしいです。
sentence.en: Everyone in the class is kind.

mnemonic.story: You dip your feet in the pond and **all** the *minnows* rush at your toes at once, a thousand tiny nibbles. Minna: all, everyone.

sentence.ja: 犬[いぬ]の{名前[なまえ]}は何[なん]ですか。
sentence.en: What's your dog's name?

mnemonic.story: Palms together, you bow: "*Namaste*." The stranger bows back and writes her **name** on your palm in ticklish felt-tip. Drop the st and you have na-ma-e: name.

sentence.ja: 田中[たなか]{さん}は先生[せんせい]ですか。
sentence.en: Is Ms. Tanaka a teacher?

mnemonic.story: Hang san after a name and it shines like a little *sun*: Tanaka-san is **Mr. or Ms.** Tanaka. Never hang it on your own name. ~San.

sentence.ja: ケンさんは十九[じゅうきゅう]{歳[さい]}です。
sentence.en: Ken is nineteen.

mnemonic.story: Blow out the birthday candles with one long *sigh*: number + sai gives **... years old**. San-sai is three years old; twenty has a word of its own, hatachi. ~Sai.

sentence.ja: 田中[たなか]さんの先生[せんせい]は{だれ}ですか。
sentence.en: Who is your teacher, Tanaka-san?

mnemonic.story: A birthday card signed "*Darren*" sits on your desk, glitter everywhere. **Who** is Darren? Nobody in the office knows a Darren. Dare: who.

sentence.ja: 部屋[へや]に学生[がくせい]が{一人[ひとり]}います。
sentence.en: There is one student in the room.

mnemonic.story: Counting people starts irregular: **one person** is hitori, built on hito, person. Picture *he* again, alone under the red torii. Not ichinin. Hito-ri: one person.

sentence.ja: 公園[こうえん]に子供[こども]が{二人[ふたり]}います。
sentence.en: There are two children in the park.

mnemonic.story: **Two people** is futari, irregular like hitori: both end in ri. Picture the pair sharing one *food tray* again. From three on, it's number plus nin. Futa-ri: two people.

sentence.ja: 子供[こども]が{三人[さんにん]}います。
sentence.en: I have three children.

mnemonic.story: From three on it's regular: san plus nin. Three *ninjas* land on the wall in a row: **three people**. San-nin: three people.

sentence.ja: 私[わたし]の家族[かぞく]は{四人[よにん]}です。
sentence.en: There are four people in my family.

mnemonic.story: Four takes the short yo, as in yoji, four o'clock: never yonnin or shinin. Four *ninjas* shout "yo!" as they land: **four people**. Yo-nin: four people.

sentence.ja: クラスに学生[がくせい]が{十五人[じゅうごにん]}います。
sentence.en: There are fifteen students in the class.

mnemonic.story: Count **people** like *ninjas* vaulting a wall: number plus nin, so san-nin, go-nin, jū-nin. Only one and two break the rule (hitori, futari), and four is yo-nin. -Nin: counter for people.

sentence.ja: {一人[ひとり]で}映画[えいが]を見[み]ました。
sentence.en: I saw a movie by myself.

mnemonic.story: Hito is person and hitori is one person; add de, "by": by one person, **alone**. The *Hee! Toe!* train is empty tonight, no stranger on your foot, just you. Hitori de.

sentence.ja: {一緒[いっしょ]に}昼[ひる]ご飯[はん]を食[た]べましょう。
sentence.en: Let's have lunch together.

mnemonic.story: In a three-legged race your knee is tied to a friend's, and you both squeal "*Eee, show knee!*" as you hobble over the line **together**. Issho ni: together.

sentence.ja: {家族[かぞく]}の写真[しゃしん]を見[み]てください。
sentence.en: Please take a look at a photo of my family.

mnemonic.story: Your whole **family** squeezes onto the sofa blowing *kazoos*, and the baby joins in at the end with a happy *coo*. Ka-zo-ku: family.

sentence.ja: {母[はは]}は毎朝[まいあさ]六時[ろくじ]に起[お]きます。
sentence.en: My mother gets up at six every morning.

mnemonic.story: Your **mother** reads your knock-knock joke and laughs, *ha ha*, two loud beats that rattle the teacups. Haha: my mother. Someone else's mother is okāsan.

sentence.ja: {父[ちち]}は毎朝[まいあさ]コーヒーを飲[の]みます。
sentence.en: My father drinks coffee every morning.

mnemonic.story: Every morning your **father** plants a scratchy, stubbly kiss on each side of your face: *cheek, cheek*. Chichi: my father. Someone else's father is otōsan.

sentence.ja: ケンさんの{お母[かあ]さん}は日本人[にほんじん]です。
sentence.en: Ken's mother is Japanese.

mnemonic.story: "*Oh, car!*" Your **mother** honks and waves from the driver's seat, the long ā like a horn. O-kā-san: mother, someone else's or what you call your own.

sentence.ja: さくらさんの{お父[とう]さん}は医者[いしゃ]ですか。
sentence.en: Is Sakura's father a doctor?

mnemonic.story: "*Oh*, my *toe*!" Your **father** stubs it on the coffee table and hops round the room. O-tō-san: father. Otōto, the little brother, has no san.

sentence.ja: {姉[あね]}は看護師[かんごし]です。
sentence.en: My older sister is a nurse.

mnemonic.story: You knock on your own **older sister**'s door and get only *a neigh* back: she still plays ponies with her daughter. Ane: my older sister.

sentence.ja: {兄[あに]}は毎日[まいにち]テニスをしています。
sentence.en: My older brother plays tennis every day.

mnemonic.story: Your own **older brother** kneels and offers *a knee* so you can climb onto his shoulders, the same knee that o-nii-san bangs on doorframes. Ani: my older brother.

sentence.ja: 山田[やまだ]さんの{お姉[ねえ]さん}は大学生[だいがくせい]です。
sentence.en: Yamada-san's older sister is a college student.

mnemonic.story: "*Oh, neigh!*" Your **older sister** gallops past on the pony, mane flying, and still won't give you a turn. O-nē-san: older sister.

sentence.ja: 田中[たなか]さんの{お兄[にい]さん}は会社員[かいしゃいん]です。
sentence.en: Tanaka-san's older brother is an office worker.

mnemonic.story: "*Oh*, my *knee*!" Your **older brother** crashes his skateboard showing off and limps home. O-nī-san: older brother. Nē for sister, nī for brother.

sentence.ja: {妹[いもうと]}は大学[だいがく]二年生[にねんせい]です。
sentence.en: My younger sister is a second-year at university.

mnemonic.story: Your **younger sister** is deep in her *emo* phase: black nail polish, black lipstick, everything she owns in one black *tote*. Imō-to: younger sister.

sentence.ja: {弟[おとうと]}の名前[なまえ]はケンです。
sentence.en: My younger brother's name is Ken.

mnemonic.story: Your **younger brother** stomps on your *toe*, then your other *toe*, and runs off giggling. O-tō-to: younger brother. Father, otō-san, keeps the san.

sentence.ja: 田中[たなか]さんは{兄弟[きょうだい]}がいますか。
sentence.en: Tanaka-san, do you have any brothers or sisters?

mnemonic.story: In *Kyoto*, all your **brothers and sisters** *dye* matching T-shirts in one big vat and come out blue to the elbows. Kyō-dai: brothers and sisters.

sentence.ja: {おじいさん}は毎朝[まいあさ]新聞[しんぶん]を読[よ]みます。
sentence.en: Grandpa reads the newspaper every morning.

mnemonic.story: Every time your phone beeps, your **grandfather** squints at it and sighs "*Oh, geee*", the gee stretched long. Short ojisan is an uncle. O-jii-san: grandfather; also any old man.

sentence.ja: {おばあさん}は猫[ねこ]が大好[だいす]きです。
sentence.en: Grandma loves cats.

mnemonic.story: Your **grandmother** knits on the porch while a sheep leans over her shoulder and comments: *oh, baaa*. Keep the baa long; short obasan is an aunt. O-bā-san: grandmother; also any old woman.

sentence.ja: 姉[あね]は来月[らいげつ]ケンさんと{結婚[けっこん]します}。
sentence.en: My older sister is marrying Ken next month.

mnemonic.story: When you **get married**, the guests throw *kettle corn* instead of rice, and it crunches under your shoes all the way down the aisle. Kekkon suru: to get married, with to marking the partner.

sentence.ja: 姉[あね]は大阪[おおさか]に{住[す]んでいます}。
sentence.en: My older sister lives in Osaka.

mnemonic.story: A *sumo* wrestler **lives** in the flat above you, and your ceiling lamp sways every time he rolls over in bed. Sum-u: to live; ni sunde imasu is "lives in".

sentence.ja: 先週[せんしゅう]、そのニュースを{知[し]りました}。
sentence.en: I found out about that news last week.

mnemonic.story: Through your *sheer* curtains you **get to know** the neighbours' whole routine: the cat at seven, the trumpet practice at nine. Shi-ru: to get to know.

sentence.ja: 田中[たなか]さんを{知[し]っています}か。
sentence.en: Do you know Tanaka-san?

mnemonic.story: Once you have peeked through the *sheer* curtains and got to know the neighbours, you **know** them: shitte imasu, the state of having got to know. Shitte imasu: I know.

sentence.ja: すみません、{知[し]りません}。
sentence.en: Sorry, I don't know.

mnemonic.story: Behind *sheer* curtains you can't see a thing, so **I don't know**. The yes is shitte imasu, but the no is plain shirimasen; nobody says shitte imasen. Shirimasen: I do not know.
